description: A saved analysis in which operators that keep their ids move one more hop and leave a new trace in their preceding slot, while each claim names that trace under an open field and an older trace of the same chain, kept unchanged in its own slot, under a source or witness field. No field names the preceding occurrence, so recovery read the older trace as the hop's source. The new trace in the moved occurrence's preceding slot is the source, whatever its field is called; the older trace is chain context. Frames are the 1-based Replay frames on 74d84eb.

cases.description: Stages 3, 5 and 10 move toughOp, firstRelOp and secondRelOp to a higher edge. Each claim names the new trace in a field without a movement role (previousEdgeTrace, edgeTrace) and an older trace in a source or witness field (objectTrace toughObjectTrace, variable firstPredTrace, variable withTrace). Every arrow started at the older trace without a transition, and each operator vanished at its stage's first frame until the claim's moment: toughOp was hidden at frames 20-39 before its moment at frame 40, firstRelOp at 53-60 and secondRelOp at 109-116. toughEdgeTrace appeared early as a selection at frame 27, frame 28 was an empty step, and the new C′ toughCProjection never appeared in stage 3.

cases.sentence: The problems that the students found easy to solve were the ones that the teacher had expected them to struggle with.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge solve with a silent object operator, and merge a silent agent PRO in the specifier of verbalizing v. Solve assigns its theme role to the operator and its agent role, through v, to PRO. This analysis uses Bare Phrase Structure: projection labels describe the results of Merge, not independently supplied phrase templates. The tough construction will have its own operator chain, distinct from the relative-clause chain. PRO's reference can be understood as the students or more generally as a contextually supplied solver; no obligatory syntactic control by the students is assumed.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the thematic domain of the tough infinitive.

values.purpose: escape from the thematic verbal domain

derivationStages.stageRecord: First internally merge the object operator at the edge of the solve vP, leaving a silent trace in its previously established object position. Then merge infinitival to and raise PRO from its thematic position to the infinitival subject position, satisfying the infinitival subject requirement. Finally merge a silent operator-selecting C. Movement is represented with traces rather than full lower copies: each trace and its continuing moved object share a lineage. The operator has not yet moved to the newly introduced CP edge.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the infinitival subject position and the tough operator's escape position.

values.interpretation: abstraction over the object of solve
the predication subject is understood as the thing to be solved

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move the tough operator from its established vP-edge position to the infinitival CP edge. Merge that CP with easy. Introduce a second silent operator as the subject of a small-clause predication whose predicate is the resulting AP. The tough dependency identifies that subject with the variable abstracted over by the infinitival operator; it does not identify the two operators as one movement chain. Merge found with this PredP and introduce the students as find's experiencer. Found is the lexically supplied past-tense form; subsequent tense licensing will check that form rather than create it by head movement.
derivationStages.statement: Build the easy predication selected by found.

values.morphologicalCommitment: lexical inflection checked without V-to-T movement

derivationStages.stageRecord: The small-clause subject receives accusative licensing from the find domain and moves to its vP edge, leaving a trace as the subject of easy. Merge silent past T, raise the students from its established thematic position to the finite subject position, and check plural agreement, nominative Case, and the past form found. Merge relative C that above TP. That is a complementizer, not the nominal operator; the operator still occupies the vP edge at this stage.
derivationStages.statement: Prepare the first finite relative clause for operator closure.

values.headAnalysis: external head with a matching relative operator
values.interpretation: problems that the students judged easy to solve

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move the first relative operator from the established find vP edge to the relative CP edge, leaving an edge trace. Adjoin the resulting restrictive CP to problems and merge the definite determiner The. The nominal head is externally merged: problems has not moved out of solve or out of the small clause. Its interpretation is supplied by the relative operator chain, whose lowest position is the subject of easy. The embedded tough chain independently supplies the object dependency of solve.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the restrictive relative modifying problems.

values.attachment: with is selected in the struggle domain

derivationStages.stageRecord: Keep the completed subject DP in the workspace. Independently merge with and a new silent relative operator, merge that PP as the complement of struggle, and introduce them as the external argument of the unergative predicate. On this ordinary reading, the relative referent is what the expected struggle concerns. Them is introduced only in the embedded thematic position; expect will not assign it a separate thematic role. Its possible reference to the students is an anaphoric interpretation, not a movement relation.
derivationStages.statement: Build struggle with as the lower predicate of the second relative.

values.dependency: extraction from the complement of with

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move the second relative operator from the established complement position of with to the edge of the struggle vP, leaving the preposition stranded. Then merge infinitival to and raise them from its thematic position to Spec-TP. This is an ECM infinitive: no CP boundary or independent nominative licenser is introduced, and them's accusative licensing remains pending until expect is merged. The infinitival subject movement satisfies the local subject requirement but does not itself value Case.
derivationStages.statement: Create the embedded infinitival subject position and strand with.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge expected with the infinitival TP, introduce verbalizing v, and merge the teacher as expect's external experiencer. The expect domain licenses accusative on them across the defective infinitival T. This is exceptional Case marking, not object control: them receives its only thematic role from struggle, while expect selects the infinitival proposition. Expected is introduced as a lexical participial form; perfect selection will be established when had is merged.
derivationStages.statement: Merge expected and license the ECM subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move the relative operator from its established embedded vP edge to the expect vP edge, crossing the defective ECM TP without an intervening CP phase. Merge had as a lexical finite perfect auxiliary in T, and raise the teacher from its external-argument position to the finite subject position. Had checks past tense, singular subject agreement and nominative Case, and selects the participial expect domain. This analysis directly merges the inflected auxiliary in T and does not posit an unrecorded auxiliary-raising step. Finally merge relative C that; the operator remains at the vP edge until the next stage.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the higher escape position and the past-perfect relative clause.

values.dependency: long-distance relative with lower preposition stranding

values.interpretation: the problems the teacher had expected them to struggle with

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move the second relative operator from the established expect vP edge to the relative CP edge. Its chain now connects the relative abstraction to the complement of the stranded preposition in the struggle domain. Attach this restrictive CP to the plural nominal proform ones and merge the definite determiner the. Ones is an overt nominal proform here; no additional silent occurrence of problems or syntactic deletion operation is required.

values.interpretation: identity of the two contextually restricted plural sets

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent predication head with the definite DP headed by ones, and merge the problems DP as the predication subject. The resulting interpretation identifies the problems described by the first relative with the set described by the second. Merge were as the lexically inflected finite copula in T. As with had, the copula is directly merged in its finite position; there is no separate lower pronounced be or unrecorded head movement. The subject remains in its previously established predication position until the next stage.

Raise the problems DP from its established PredP-subject position to the matrix finite subject position, leaving a silent trace. Were agrees with this plural subject, checks its nominative Case, and supplies matrix past tense. Merge a silent declarative C. The completed tree pronounces the exact input in order. The two relative operators, the tough operator, PRO, traces and abstract functional heads are silent. No realization mapping is necessary because all overt lexical forms were retained directly. This reading locates with inside the expected struggle: the teacher expected difficulty with those problems.
